newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF to pay dividends, approves $1.0 bln bond issue.
newsitem.headline: YPF to pay dividends, approves $1.0 bln bond issue.

text.p: Argentine oil company YPF SA said its annual shareholders meeting Tuesday approved a $78 million first quarter cash dividend to be paid in May.
That dividend is 10 percent higher than any quarterly dividend paid so far, the company said in a press release.
YPF also said it will pay $233 million in three quarterly dividends totalling $0.66 per share in August and November 1997 and February 1998.
It added shareholders approved a new $1.0 billion negotiable bond program. Last year it approved a separate $500 million negotiable bond program.
Proceeds from the program will be used for, among other things, fixed asset investments within Argentina and to refinance debt and inject capital to companies it controls or has interests.
The negotiable bonds could be issued with or without collateral.
The company also said it would earmark $21 million to set up a fund for future dividends.
The shareholders meeting approved the remaining $1.18 billion in retained earnings by December 31, 1996, be transferred to the new fiscal year.

Shareholders also approved the nomination of Roberto Monti as executive vice president and CEO to replace outgoing president Nells Leon in all his executive functions. Leon will remain as a member of the board.
Monti has been president and general manager of YPF's wholly owned subsidiary Maxus since 1995.
Executive vice Presidente Miguel Madanes was named president. From now on that job will have mostly protocol responsibilities, a YPF source said.
Leon said that in 1996 YPF redeemed a substantial part of Maxus preferred stock and that it has made early payments on part of the debt taken up to buy that company.
He added that in the next fiscal year YPF expected to reach higher oil and natural gas output levels and keep improving its international operations.
